source_name: Državna revizorska institucija Crne Gore (DRI) — revizorski izvještaji
why_relevant: Supreme audit institution reports on individual spending units (e.g. Uprava prihoda i carina, agencies) routinely itemise procurement contracts, bank account arrangements, treasury banking and payment-service costs, and criticise irregular awards. Audits reveal contract detail and vendor relationships that award notices compress or omit, and DRI has run a regional performance audit on procurement efficiency.

source_name: gov.me — Javne nabavke pages of ministries and administrations (whole-of-government hub)
source_subtype: government portal buyer pages / procurement plans
why_relevant: Each ministry/administration publishes its plan javnih nabavki and contract list on its gov.me subsite (e.g. Ministarstvo javne uprave tenderi library). Annual procurement PLANS are the highest-value forward-looking artefact in this cell: they disclose intended banking/payment/IT purchases months before any notice.

source_name: Nabavke.com — regional tender aggregator, Montenegro section
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator that indexes Montenegrin notices with stable per-tender URLs including buyer name and city (observed: CBCG printing services, Pošta Crne Gore office materials). Useful as a redundant, more crawler-friendly mirror of CEJN and for historical notices that may have rotated off the official portal.

source_name: Javne-nabavke.com — Montenegro tender monitoring service
why_relevant: States explicitly that it monitors CEJN plus additional sources for Montenegro and publishes market statistics (approx. 4,000 tenders/year, average estimated value ~EUR 228k, ~24 days to bid). Useful both as a redundant feed and as a source of denominator statistics for sizing the ME public-procurement channel.

source_name: eKapija — Tenderi / pretraga tendera (regional business portal)
why_relevant: Regional business-news portal with a tender search covering Montenegro; pairs procurement items with editorial coverage, which is the cheapest way to spot a tender that has news significance (new bank, new payment scheme, ATM network change) rather than routine supplies.

source_name: eTenderi.me — Montenegrin tender listing service
why_relevant: Domestic .me tender listing surfaced alongside the official portal in local-language search; potential secondary mirror for ME notices. Low prior on completeness and unclear operator, so it is a lead to evaluate rather than a trusted feed.

source_name: EEAS / Delegation of the EU to Montenegro — calls for tender and service contract award notices
why_relevant: The EU Delegation publishes its own contract notices and 'Obavještenje o dodjeli ugovora o uslugama' (service contract award notices) for IPA-funded technical assistance in Montenegro — including public finance management, digitalisation and financial-sector reform assignments that shape later national tenders.

source_name: EIB — project procurement and EIB Group Supplier Portal
why_relevant: EIB-financed ME operations (and EIB technical assistance designing procurement approaches for ME public bodies) generate notices under the EIB Guide to Procurement. Relevant where EIB co-finances state digitalisation or SOE investment with a payments component; also a route to identify which ME entities are borrowing.

source_name: MANS — Javne nabavke monitoring (Balkan Tender Watch)
why_relevant: Investigative NGO that monitors Montenegrin procurement and publishes institution profiles and case analyses (including on the procurement review commission). Surfaces contested or opaque awards and beneficial-ownership links that neither CEJN nor DRI state plainly — an early-warning layer over the official record.

source_name: MONSTAT — published procurement decisions (odluka o izboru) and Zakon o javnim nabavkama text (Paragraf.me)
why_relevant: Consolidated legal text of the Law on Public Procurement defines which documents must be published, when, and in what form (plan, tender notice, odluka o izboru, ugovor, izvještaj o izvršenju) — the schema on which any collection pipeline for this cell must be built. MONSTAT's published 'odluka o izboru' PDF is a concrete example of the older Obrazac-based document format still found on institution sites.

source_name: Payten — News & Events (vendor go-live press releases, ASEE Group payments arm)
why_relevant: Payten (ASEE Group) is the dominant regional ATM/POS/e-commerce vendor for SEE. Its news feed carries named Montenegrin go-lives — e.g. a confirmed release 'Payten Implemented SoftPOS Solution in Hipotekarna banka in Montenegro'. This is the single richest vendor-side trace of who bought what in ME cards/acceptance.

source_name: MoneyGet Crna Gora (Asseco/Payten independent ATM network, ME entity site)
source_subtype: vendor country subsidiary / network operator site
why_relevant: MoneyGet is Payten/ASEE's own ATM network operating in Montenegro. Its site reveals ATM estate footprint, partner banks and acquiring arrangements — an indirect read on which ME banks outsource cash-out and to whom.

source_name: ASEE / Asseco South Eastern Europe — corporate site (solutions, references, investor reporting)
why_relevant: ASEE is the parent of Payten and of the e-banking products used by ME banks. Its corporate site plus WSE-listed investor materials aggregate segment/market commentary and occasionally name SEE bank clients; it is the umbrella pointer behind several ME-specific traces (E-mon Podgorica, MoneyGet ME, Payten ME).

source_name: E-mon / Servisni centar e-mon (ASEE electronic-banking service centre, Podgorica)
source_subtype: vendor service-centre site / implicit client list
why_relevant: E-mon is the ASEE-affiliated Podgorica service centre for electronic banking / digital certificates, present in ME since 2004. Its client/support pages effectively enumerate which Montenegrin banks run ASEE e-banking (Hal/E-mon Web stack) — a de facto vendor reference list for digital channels.

source_name: Qualys Customer Success Stories — Crnogorska Komercijalna Banka (CKB) case study
why_relevant: A named, vendor-published case study on Montenegro's largest bank (CKB, OTP Group). Confirms the security-tooling supplier and typically discloses estate size, architecture hints and drivers — exactly the procurement trace ME's private banks never publish themselves.

source_name: Printec Montenegro d.o.o. — country site (transaction automation vendor)
why_relevant: Printec has operated in ME since 2014 in transaction automation (ATM/self-service/POS) with service centres in Podgorica, Ulcinj and Budva. The country page and group newsroom are the vendor-side index of ME bank relationships and service footprint.

source_name: Halcom — list of banks using Halcom (e-banking client index)
why_relevant: Halcom publishes an explicit, maintained list of banks running its Hal E-Bank corporate e-banking and qualified-certificate stack across the ex-YU region. Where Montenegrin banks appear, this is a direct vendor-confirmed client mapping for corporate digital channels.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. (Ljubljana) — card/ATM/POS processing bureau
why_relevant: Bankart is the NLB Group-associated processing bureau (NLB holds c.40%) serving card, ATM and POS processing for member banks. For NLB Banka Podgorica and other ME clients, Bankart's company/why-Bankart pages and NLB Group pages are the vendor-side evidence of who processes ME card traffic.

source_name: Čikom d.o.o. (Podgorica) — ICT integrator, project/reference pages and LinkedIn feed
why_relevant: Čikom is described as a leading ME ICT company and digital-transformation integrator, appearing in national consortium projects (e.g. eKomora). Its reference/news output is a pointer to infrastructure and systems delivered into ME financial institutions.

source_name: Softing d.o.o. (ME) — eCommerce integrations page (payment-gateway/acquirer integration list)
why_relevant: A Montenegrin software house publishing which bank e-commerce gateways it integrates with. Vendor-side integration lists reveal which acquiring banks and which gateway platforms are live in ME — a rare, concrete acceptance-side pointer.

source_name: Agilcon (Salesforce Platinum partner) — Lovćen Banka portfolio entry
why_relevant: A named vendor portfolio page for a Montenegrin bank (Lovćen Banka), evidencing CRM/Salesforce-side adoption. Confirms the pattern that ME bank procurement surfaces only on the supplier's portfolio page.

source_name: Gecko HRM — Lovćen Banka case study
why_relevant: Named vendor case study on a ME bank (HR/compliance systems). Low strategic value on its own but valuable as a confirmed data point in the vendor-reference index and for mapping the bank's internal digitalisation programme and named executives.

source_name: Google Play / Apple App Store listings for ME bank apps (developer field as vendor tell)
why_relevant: App-store metadata leaks the actual builder of a bank's mobile channel: the Adriatic Bank ME app is published under an 'abctechgroup' package id, and regional Asseco-built apps carry 'hr.asseco.android.*' package ids. Package namespace, developer name and release cadence are a reliable, machine-readable vendor fingerprint where no press release exists.

source_name: One Crna Gora (Telekom Austria Group) — data centre / telehousing customer announcements
source_subtype: vendor-customer joint press release (via national media)
why_relevant: Joint vendor-customer announcement naming Hipotekarna banka's telehousing/data-centre supplier, quoting the bank's Director of Support, Organisation and Digital Transformation on the selection process. Infrastructure-supplier announcements are a recurring ME channel for procurement disclosure.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf — banking customer success stories / case study index
why_relevant: Global self-service/ATM vendor whose case-study index is the canonical place a Montenegrin ATM estate deal would surface. No ME entry was found in this pass, but the index must be monitored as a standing pointer for the ATM/POS vendor cell.

source_name: AppsRunTheWorld customer databases (Diebold Nixdorf, Oracle FLEXCUBE, etc.)
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator that compiles vendor customer lists per product. Useful as a cross-check index to test whether any ME bank appears against core-banking / self-service products, and to generate candidate vendor-bank pairs for targeted verification.

source_name: Cuspera vendor customer-story aggregator (Temenos and peers)
why_relevant: Aggregates published vendor customer stories in one searchable place, cheaper to sweep than crawling every core-banking vendor site individually. Serves as a discovery net for any future ME core-banking reference.

source_name: Ziraat Bank Montenegro — e-banking general terms PDF naming Asseco SEE as producer
source_subtype: bank legal document (T&C PDF) disclosing vendor
why_relevant: Bank-published terms-of-use documents routinely name the software producer of the e-banking application (here: Asseco SEE / E-mon Web). Contract and T&C PDFs are an underused, highly reliable vendor-attribution channel where no case study exists.
